R276 — Audit of the proposed H2D memcpy2d cohort against the Level Zero V2 adapter
Date: 2026-10-12

Scope and identity

This is a read-only source audit, not a performance result. I inspected the pinned Intel LLVM tree `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/intel/llvm/.worktree/toolchain-sycl-v711-b570-20261011` at HEAD `504366f4b8`. This source snapshot is distinct from the deployed Intel oneAPI 2025.1.1 package, reported as DPC++/SYCL 7.1.1, libSYCL ABI 9.0.0, with `libur_adapter_level_zero_v2.so.0.12.0`. The checkout explains the matching implementation path; it alone does not prove the installed binary was built from this exact tree. The source files below were read directly; hashes are recorded at the end.

Finding

For the proposed host-USM source to device-USM destination, `sycl_ext_oneapi_memcpy2d` takes the native USM 2D special-command path in this SYCL implementation. The Level Zero V2 adapter appends `zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopyRegion`; it does not launch a GPU fallback kernel for this case. That is a hardware copy-region command submission. It does not prove which physical engine the driver executes it on, nor that the driver actually overlaps it with compute.

The SYCL extension's plain `ext_oneapi_memcpy2d` handler classifies both pointers. Both-host pointers use a host task. If either pointer is host (including this host-USM source), or the backend reports native USM 2D support, it calls `ext_oneapi_memcpy2d_impl`; only the remaining device-only/non-native case takes the kernel fallback (`sycl/include/sycl/ext/oneapi/memcpy2d.hpp:36-58`). The handler records `CGType::Copy2DUSM` and preserves destination pitch, source pitch, width, and height (`sycl/source/handler.cpp:991-1002`). The queue overloads accept one event or a vector and put those dependencies on the handler (header lines 146-171). The extension specification defines pitches and width in bytes and copies `width * height` bytes/rows, with width no greater than either pitch; both pointers must be host pointers or USM accessible from the queue's device and context. See [SYCL oneAPI memcpy2d extension source](https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/504366f4b8/sycl/doc/extensions/supported/sycl_ext_oneapi_memcpy2d.asciidoc).

The V2 command-list manager's `appendUSMMemcpy2D` wraps the raw pointers in USM handles, uses zero origins and region `{width,height,0}`, and forwards the two pitches. `appendRegionCopyUnlocked` converts them to Level Zero region parameters, obtains the underlying pointers, gets the requested signal event, and directly invokes `zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopyRegion`, forwarding wait handles and signal event. With `blocking=false`, it does not host-synchronize there (`unified-runtime/source/adapters/level_zero/v2/command_list_manager.cpp:191-221,574-590`). This corresponds to the Level Zero API's documented region copy for host/device/shared memory; region width, height, and depth must match for source and destination, and source/destination regions must not overlap. [Level Zero command-list specification](https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/latest/core/api/apis/command_list.html).

Geometry and bounds

For R273's fixed-stride rows, the intended parameters are valid in shape when `width=blob_bytes`, `srcPitch=blob_bytes`, `dstPitch=MMQ_SLOT()`, and `height=cohort_count`; `width <= both pitches` is required and also checked synchronously by the SYCL handler. The useful byte span is `(height - 1) * pitch + width` for each side (zero if height is zero). The adapter's `ur2zeRegionParams` narrows width, height, and pitches to `uint32_t` (`helpers/memory_helpers.cpp`), so every passed width, height, and pitch must be <= `UINT32_MAX`; validate before narrowing and check multiplication/addition overflow. V2's USM handles are constructed with size zero, and the plain USM `getDevicePtr` path returns the raw pointer rather than validating that the full rectangular span fits an allocation. The wrapper therefore must prove source and destination extents itself, including allocation identity/offset, ring slot range, no wrap in a rectangle, and non-overlap. Do not batch across layer boundaries, skipped/resident holes, transient/stager memory, ring wrap, or any source span whose host-USM contiguity/lifetime is not proven. Retain the existing individual-copy fallback for every ineligible case.

Event, completion, and error handling

A dependency vector becomes SYCL handler dependencies, then UR wait-list events. V2 `appendRegionCopyUnlocked` passes that list to the Level Zero append operation and associates the caller's signal event with the command. The queue's normal returned event therefore denotes completion of the one region operation, not separate completion for each row. It is sound for all cohort members only if every member's prior last-reader (`used`) event is included as a dependency and consumers wait on that cohort event before reading any member. Keep per-slot last-reader events and slot-credit/reuse rules unchanged. Preserve async errors: submit through the normal queue API, use an async handler, and drain with event/queue `wait_and_throw`; don't treat enqueue success or a signaled host-side submission as successful device completion. The V2 source path itself does not add a synchronous host completion for nonblocking copies. The API docs note graph-associated memcpy2d is unsupported; do not issue this path from a SYCL Graph.

Copy-engine offload

Both immediate in-order and batched V2 queue descriptors request copy offload in this source tree. `command_list_cache.cpp` reads `UR_L0_V2_FORCE_DISABLE_COPY_OFFLOAD` once into a static setting. When set, it clears the requested-offload state. When the driver supports the Level Zero copy-offload queue flag, this removes `ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_FLAG_COPY_OFFLOAD_HINT`; otherwise the V2 path uses the queue-copy-offload extension property with `copyOffloadEnabled=false` (`command_list_cache.cpp:88-130`). This is a queue/driver hint control. It does not change the 2D command into a fallback kernel and does not guarantee physical copy-engine selection either way. Because the setting is cached, compare enabled/disabled only in separate fresh processes. Verify the actual selected UR adapter and runtime logs on the deployed package before claiming this source behavior matches the installed library.

Safe first GPU fixture (no model)

Use a standalone small SYCL program on the intended device with an async handler, host-USM source and device-USM destination allocated in the same context. Exercise a matrix of row widths, unequal pitches, heights (including 1), and several destination offsets; initialize source row payload and padding with distinct sentinels and verify copied payload plus untouched destination padding after `wait_and_throw`. Include a two-queue producer -> copy -> consumer dependency chain, and a cohort whose destination-slot reuse events are all dependencies; verify exact payload and that no slot is read before the cohort completion. Include boundary-rejection checks in the wrapper for overflow, >UINT32_MAX geometry, undersized allocations, and ring wrap without actually issuing an invalid Level Zero call. Run offload enabled and `UR_L0_V2_FORCE_DISABLE_COPY_OFFLOAD=1` in separate processes, and confirm correct results and async-error propagation in both. Record device/driver/runtime package identity and raw correctness outcomes. Only after that, use a clean, non-validation performance comparison with the existing one-copy-per-expert implementation; the current measurement is explicitly not performance eligible.

Evidence and limits

The previously closed R273 receipt establishes 509 copies per layer per chunk, 48 layers, 4 chunks: 97,728 H2D calls and 199,990,579,200 submitted bytes. It is correctness evidence for the current path, not for memcpy2d and not for speed. This audit validates that the proposed host-USM to device-USM rectangular command can reach the Level Zero V2 region-copy entrypoint under the audited source; it does not establish runtime/package identity, correct integration in Strata, speedup, actual DMA/copy-engine selection, reduced physical bytes, or overlap. No implementation or GPU run was performed.
